CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE N S SANJAY GOWDA  -3-  NC: 2024:KHC:51089  MFA No. 3275 of 2020  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.
The claimants, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.35,68,300/- awarded by the Tribunal for the death of one Mohiddin Sharif, are in appeal.

sentences.text:
It is not in dispute that as a result of the motor vehicle accident which occurred on 08.02.2018,
Mohiddin Sharif, a 49 year old died.
3. The liability of the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation ("KSRTC") to pay the compensation is also not in dispute.

4. The main grievance put forth by the claimants in this appeal is that the pay-slips which were produced indicate that the deceased was consistently getting an overtime pay and this aspect of the matter has been disregarded by the Tribunal on the basis of a ruling of the Division Bench of this Court, which is improper.
It is also sought to be contented the NC: 2024:KHC:51089 amount awarded towards loss of consortium would be incorrect.

5. Admittedly, the deceased was a driver in KSRTC and the Tribunal has recorded a finding that as on the date of his death, as per Exhibit P-22/pay slip, he was getting a net salary of Rs.25,877/- for the month of January-2018.

6. The Tribunal has disregarded the claim for over-time allowance on the basis of the decisions rendered by Division Bench of this Court in the cases of Girja1 and Lalithamma2.
7.

As far as the judgments of the Division Bench are concerned, it is noticed that it was not a case in which the claimants had pleaded and established that the deceased was consistently getting an over-time allowance.

In that view of the matter, the said judgments cannot be relied upon for the proposition Smt.Girija and another vs. Shivakumar and others, ILR 2009 KAR 979 The Managing Director, KSRTC vs. Lalithamma and others, 2010 ACJ 1018.
NC: 2024:KHC:51089 that over-time allowance cannot be taken into consideration while computing the monthly income.

entities.text: Smt.Girija and another vs. Shivakumar and others, ILR 2009 KAR 979
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Managing Director, KSRTC vs. Lalithamma and others, 2010 ACJ 1018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
8. In the instant case, the claimants have produced the pay-slips for the years 2015, 2016 and 2017,
i.e., for three years preceding the date of the accident.
The pay-slips which were produced indicate that for the year 2015, the deceased was drawing an average salary of Rs.28,018/- per month.
For the year 2016, he was earning Rs.33,504/- and for the year 2017, he was earning Rs.37,677/-.
It is therefore clear that the claimant was consistently getting almost 15% to 20% above his net salary as over-time allowance.

9. If the deceased was consistently getting an overtime allowance, it is obvious that the KSRTC was suffering a shortage of drivers and consequently the drivers who were working were asked to work overtime.
If this overtime is established to be prevailing for more NC: 2024:KHC:51089 than three years, in my view, this component cannot be disregarded.

10. Having taken into consideration that the above sums indicate the average monthly salary, in my view, interest of justice would be served by taking the average monthly income of the deceased as Rs.29,000/-.

sentences.text: As per the decision of the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi3, as the deceased was aged about 49 years and was on permanent employment, 30% of the aforesaid salary income (Rs.8,700/-.) is required to be added to it as future prospects and the resultant income would be Rs.37,700/-.

12. Since the deceased's wife and two children were the only dependents, out of the said sum, 1/3rd of the same (Rs.12,567/-) would have to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased. The net income will be Rs.25,133/-.

National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others - (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC:
2024:KHC:51089 13.

2024:KHC:51089
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As the deceased was aged 49 years, as per the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma4, a multiplier of '13' would have to be applied.
14. Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.39,20,748/- (Rs.25,133/- x 12 x '13') towards "loss of dependency".

15. As the father is no more, the claimants being the wife, two children and mother, as per Pranay Sethi5, they would each be entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/- towards "loss of love and affection"
i.e., in all Rs.1,93,600/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.36,300/-
under "conventional heads".

16. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums :

A sum of Rs.15,000/- paid to the claimants as ex gratia and a sum of Rs.6,25,880/-
compensation paid under the Employees Compensation Act shall be deducted from the said amount.

19. The KSRTC is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded along with interest within a NC: 2024:KHC:51089 period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

20. On such deposit, out of the compensation and interest, 10% of the same is apportioned in favour of the mother; 40% is apportioned in favour of the wife; and 25% each is apportioned in favour of the two children of the deceased.
21. The deposit and release of the enhanced compensation amount shall be made as per the ratio adopted by the Tribunal.
22. The entire compensation amount apportioned in favour of the mother deceased shall be released in her favour on proper identification.
23. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
